21:42.sourceText: Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας· παρὰ Κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη, καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν;
21:42.targetText: Jesus says to them, “Did you never read in the Writings: A stone that the builders disallowed, it became head of a corner; from the LORD has this come to pass, and it is wonderful in our eyes?

groups.note: The actual stone noun is accusative as the quoted clause’s fronted relative antecedent; English presents A stone as the topic. Its Greek case remains accusative rather than silently changed to nominative.
The actual becoming verb with its εἰς result marker supplies became in became head. English absorbs the result relation into the becoming predicate rather than adding a separate into word.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before Jesus is not separately expressed in English.

21:43.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἀρθήσεται ἀφ’ ὑμῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ δοθήσεται ἔθνει ποιοῦντι τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῆς.
21:43.targetText: Because of this I say to you that the Kingdom of God will be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth its fruit;

groups.note: The actual source καρπούς is plural fruits; LSV uses the collective/mass singular fruit for that same produce. Its written Greek plural remains visible.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with its fruit.

21:44.sourceText: καὶ ὁ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὸν λίθον τοῦτον συνθλασθήσεται· ἐφ’ ὃν δ’ ἂν πέσῃ, λικμήσει αὐτόν.
21:44.targetText: and he who is falling on this stone will be broken, and on whomsoever it may fall it will crush him to pieces.”

groups.note: The actual πεσών is an aorist falling participle, rendered progressive is falling by LSV. The English auxiliary belongs to that real fall predicate; the source is not a present Greek participle.

The actual λικμάω is a winnowing/scattering/crushing predicate, rendered crush ... to pieces in this stone image. No separately printed pieces noun or different crushing lemma is invented (Mounce, λικμάω).

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with this stone.

21:45.sourceText: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὰς παραβολὰς αὐτοῦ ἔγνωσαν ὅτι περὶ αὐτῶν λέγει·
21:45.targetText: And the chief priests and the Pharisees having heard His allegories, knew that He speaks of them,

groups.note: The actual παραβολή parable/comparison noun is rendered allegories by this edition; the source lemma is not a separate ἀλληγορία noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His allegories.

21:46.sourceText: καὶ ζητοῦντες αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι ἐφοβήθησαν τοὺς ὄχλους, ἐπεὶ εἰς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον.
21:46.targetText: and seeking to lay hold on Him, they feared the multitudes, seeing they were holding Him as a prophet.
